questions.modelAnswer:
Site, blood supply and effect of lesion of: (1) Auditory area (areas 41,42) – in the superior temporal gyrus (Heschl's gyri); supplied by the middle cerebral artery; a unilateral lesion causes only partial (bilateral) hearing impairment because of the bilateral representation, while bilateral lesions cause cortical deafness. questions.text: Name and locate the speech centers. (3 Marks)
questions.explanation: Language depends on cortical areas usually located in the dominant (left) hemisphere. Broca's area in the inferior frontal gyrus programs the motor production of speech, while Wernicke's area in the temporoparietal region governs comprehension.
